name: 1.1.87 — the tutor HAS the task, and it is the right one
description: Behavioural gate for 1.1.87 (activity-task-materials-in-context), from item 1 of the 2026-08-21 teacher feedback. A teacher built a lesson on 'students work past Physics A exam questions with the tutor', cited the papers as materials, and the tutor asked students to paste the task in — then discussed a DIFFERENT paper's Question 5. The deterministic half (the text reaches llm_request.contents at all) is pinned by tests/tool_tests/test_activity_document_callbacks.py, which runs in CI. THIS half is the model-behaviour claim and only an eval can hold it: run with `make eval EVALSET=tests/eval/evalsets/activity_task_in_context.evalset.json` (GCP credentials required); NOT part of make test-fast. Setup required before running: an activity with TWO context materials, each an exam paper containing a question numbered 5, cited as kind="context".

eval_cases.description: The reported failure, first half: the tutor 'still asked students to upload the assignment text'. One opening message, no mention of a file. The tutor must engage with the task it was given and must NOT ask the student to paste or upload it.

parts.text: Hej, jeg er gået i gang med opgaven. Hvad går den ud på?

eval_cases.description: The reported failure, second half, and the load-bearing case: 'it talking about a completely different Question 5 when made aware it had the file'. Two papers are in context, each with a Question 5. Asked about Question 5 of the NAMED paper, the tutor must discuss that paper's question — the failure this reproduces is confident wrongness the student cannot detect.

parts.text: Kan du hjælpe mig med opgave 5 i sættet fra maj 2019?

eval_cases.description: Open question 1 of the design doc, in behavioural form. With several papers in context, a bare 'question 5' is genuinely ambiguous. The tutor must ASK WHICH — picking one silently is how the original bug reads to a student. This is the case that says whether M3 (task selection) is needed or whether asking is enough.

The Axiom 4 bound, behaviourally. An over-cap material is inlined head-plus-tail with the middle marked missing. Asked about something in the omitted middle, the tutor must say it cannot see that part rather than answering from the half it has — the same class of confident wrongness, reintroduced by the fix if the flag is ignored.
